description.title: Sun Geocentric Position
description.what: Computes astrometric geocentric RA/Dec of the Sun at given epochs. Accuracy reference is JPL Horizons (astrometric geocentric, ICRF, Earth geocenter, TT).
description.why: Sun position is needed for solar observations, shadow calculations, and as input to other transforms.
description.units: Angular separation in arcseconds between JPL Horizons reference and candidate Sun positions.
description.interpret: Lower error = closer to JPL Horizons DE441 ephemeris. All libraries are compared as candidates against the Horizons reference.
description.performance_contract: Timed scope: ephemeris evaluation per epoch (no I/O). Input JD parsing and output formatting are outside the timed loop. libnova pre-computes VSOP87 helio position outside the timed loop; siderust constructs frame objects inside the timed loop.

alignment.time_input: JD (Julian Date), TT scale for precession/nutation, UT1 for sidereal time
alignment.time_scales: TT for BPN matrix; UT1≈TT-69.184s simplified
alignment.leap_seconds: not applicable (JD input, no UTC conversion in this experiment)
alignment.ephemeris_source: JPL Horizons (DE441) for reference; VSOP87/SPK for candidates

library_notes.astropy: The 'astropy' adapter uses public Astropy Time and SkyCoord APIs. Astropy may use ERFA internally, but this adapter no longer calls ERFA/pyerfa kernels directly.

models.jpl_horizons: JPL Horizons geometric VECTORS (DE441, ICRF, VEC_CORR=NONE, Earth geocenter, TT)
models.erfa: VSOP87 via eraEpv00: heliocentric Earth → geocentric Sun (negate); BCRS equatorial output
models.siderust: Geometric heliocentric-ecliptic center transformed to geocentric ICRS (no aberration)
models.libnova: VSOP87 geometric (ln_get_solar_geo_coords; heliocentric + geocentric rectangular vectors; no nutation/aberration)
models.anise: SPK translation SUN_J2000 → EARTH_J2000 (DE440 ephemeris, geometric state vector)

alignment.accuracy_interpretation: agreement with JPL Horizons geometric VECTORS reference (no aberration / nutation)
alignment.note: Public geometric lane — JPL VECTORS (no aberration, no light-time, no nutation). Ranked as best-available model vs JPL reference: same observable, different physical models (libnova VSOP87 geometric, siderust DE441/DE440/VSOP87 best-available, ANISE SPK).

warnings: High coefficient of variation (41.3%). Results are unstable. Consider increasing sample count or reducing system load.
